title: Keep optimistic presentation separate from authoritative state
businessContext: Review a focused Next.js application change before it reaches production. The proposed file below contains the defect or unsupported assumption; external application services, where imported, are integration boundaries.
problemStatement: Review the proposed app/messages.tsx change. Identify the incorrect framework assumption, propose a minimal corrected implementation, and provide evidence for the selected version scope and its 15/16 differences. Explain the interview variation after solving the base task. This is a framework code review: actual rendering, routing and cache behavior must be checked in a real Next.js build, not a browser function sandbox.
constraints: Preserve the stated user behavior and keep trust boundaries explicit.
Use the selected version’s documented API; do not suppress build/type failures to hide the defect.
Send a successful message and reconcile server props.
Reject a send and verify the temporary result is not treated as durable.
Admit identical concurrent messages with distinct operation IDs before using the pattern in production.
candidateTasks: Add actionable line-level review comments explaining impact and correction.
Write the corrected file in the local IDE copy; split annotated companion files where instructed.
Record actual build/request/navigation evidence against the acceptance checks and compare version notes.
hints: React owns the DOM, so mutating innerHTML bypasses reconciliation and injects untrusted text.
Send a successful message and reconcile server props.
alternativeApproaches: Model draft/error state separately from the optimistic projection. Associate an operation ID with the retry policy and avoid appending the same authoritative message twice when the original result arrives late.
commonMistakes: Verifying only next dev when the behavior depends on production rendering or bundling.
Treating a visible UI state, matcher or TypeScript type as a substitute for server-side validation and authorization.
